sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 of the August 1920 Hackensack volume, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the northern part of the Borough of Bogota and the adjoining strip of Teaneck Township, from Kipp at the top of the sheet to South at the bottom. The township boundary crosses the sheet diagonally between Hillside and Homestead Place and is lettered Teaneck Township above and Borough of Bogota below. River Road runs down the left side, slightly angled, with houses on its west side facing the Hackensack River, which is not drawn (the margin is marked no exposure). East of River Road the blocks are laid out on a regular grid of north-south avenues (Catalpa, Larch, Elm and Linden avenues and Chestnut Place) and cross streets (Kipp, Oritani Place, Terhune, Centre Place, Hillside, Homestead Place, West Grove, Park Place and South). Most lots are narrow and many are still vacant, especially in the township blocks at the top; the built lots carry one- and two-storey frame dwellings with private garages. A few hollow tile and stuccoed houses are shown, a fire alarm box stands at River Road and Park Place, and the Bogota Embroidery Co. embroidery shop stands on Elm Avenue near the bottom. A six-inch water pipe of the Hackensack Water Co. is drawn along several streets. Lane and Riverside Park are short streets running west from River Road toward the river, and Atkinson Place runs south from Park Place. At the lower right the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad (West Shore) tracks cross the corner, with Leonia Avenue and Lookout Street beyond them. Sheets 37, 41, 31 and 32 adjoin at the top, left, right and bottom.
notes: Hillside is now Hillcrest Street; Centre Place is Center Place; Kipp and Terhune are Kipp Street and Terhune Street.
Linden Avenue is Linden Street north of the junction near Hillcrest Street in OpenStreetMap.
River Road junctions sat 3 to 7.5 m off the fit and were left out; the modern road appears widened or realigned.
Catalpa junctions at Kipp and Terhune were rejected (11 to 14 m off).

River Road left out (junctions 3 to 7.5 m off). Old names: Hillside = Hillcrest Street, Centre Pl = Center Place, Terhune = Terhune Street.

sheet-31-1.description: Main part of sheet 31 of the August 1920 Hackensack volume, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It shows the eastern part of the Borough of Bogota between the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad (West Shore) and the Teaneck Township line, from Karet at the top to Degraw Avenue at the bottom, with Leonia Avenue running diagonally along the railroad and Palisade Avenue down the middle. The cross streets are Karet, Grove, Cane, Lookout, Highwood, East Broad and Highview Place. The blocks are divided into narrow house lots, about half of them built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, some stuccoed or of hollow tile, and many private garages; a fire alarm box stands at Palisade Avenue and Lookout. The township boundary runs along the top of the built blocks and down the east side as a dash-dot line, and the blocks east of Palisade Avenue are only partly subdivided. North of the boundary, beside the railroad, is the Bogota shop of the Raymond Concrete Pile Co., a fire-resistive machine shop of reinforced concrete with storage sheds, a derrick and a hoisting engine. At the top left corner the ends of Terhune and Chestnut Place repeat the edge of sheet 30, and Linden is lettered at the left margin. The upper right of the sheet, inside a heavy line, is a separately oriented inset (part 2). Sheets 30 and 33 adjoin at the left and bottom.
notes: Karet is now Pine Street, Lookout is Gray Street, and Highwood is Kovar Street (Henry C Luthin Place east of Palisade Avenue).
Raymond Concrete Pile Co., Bogota Shop, beside the railroad.

Printed sheet 31, 100 ft. Part 1: Bogota east of the railroad (Leonia and Palisade avenues, Karet to Degraw) plus the Raymond Concrete Pile Co shop and Terhune/Chestnut Place top left. Part 2: inset inside a heavy line, turned about 70 degrees: Paradise Farm horse training stables at Queen Anne Road and Cedar Lane, anchored on its one junction. Old names: Karet = Pine Street, Lookout = Gray Street, Highwood = Kovar Street.

sheet-31-2.description: Inset in the upper right of sheet 31 of the August 1920 Hackensack volume, set off from the main map by a heavy line and drawn turned on the page: its north arrow points to the upper right, so Queen Anne Road, lettered across the bottom of the inset, runs roughly north-south and Cedar Lane, lettered up the right side, runs east-west. The scale is the sheet's 100 feet to an inch. Most of the inset is taken up by Paradise Farm, horse training stables, in Teaneck Township: a large one-and-a-half-storey stable or riding building with a cross-braced roof, a garage with a cement floor and a buried 180-gallon gasoline tank, a greenhouse, sheds and a few dwellings, with a dimension of 330 feet marked from the top margin, which is lettered no exposure. A 30-inch water pipe runs along Queen Anne Road and a six-inch and a 30-inch pipe along Cedar Lane, with a hydrant at their corner. East of Cedar Lane a few scattered dwellings, a dairy and outbuildings are drawn. The inset has only one street junction, Queen Anne Road and Cedar Lane, so its placement rests on that point and on the assumed scale.
notes: Placed from a single junction (Queen Anne Road / Cedar Lane) with the rotation from its drawn lines and the scale of the main part; low confidence away from that corner.

sheet-37-1.description: Left half of sheet 37 of the August 1920 Hackensack volume, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and divided from the right half by a heavy vertical line. It covers part of Teaneck Township east of Queen Anne Road, from Degraw Avenue at the top to Maple at the bottom. In the upper part, Beech, Chestnut and Elm run up from the Hackensack & Fort Lee Road, which crosses the sheet diagonally; these blocks are drawn at a slight angle to the grid below and are mostly subdivided but vacant, except for a row of new dwellings along Elm. South of the Fort Lee Road a large block holds a garage of cement and tile, an auto supply building and greenhouses. Below Munn Avenue the streets form a regular grid: Munn Avenue, Sherwood Avenue, Walnut, Oak and Maple crossed by Bergen Avenue, Park Avenue and Lees Avenue, with large lots and scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, many with garages. A 30-inch water pipe runs along Walnut, marked to New Durham station, and six-inch pipes along most other streets. The lots along the left margin continue on sheet 34, which adjoins at the top.
notes: Chestnut is now Woodbine Street and Elm is Morningside Terrace; Walnut, Oak and Maple are Walnut Street, Oak Street and Maple Street; the Hackensack & Fort Lee Road is Fort Lee Road.
Park Avenue ends at Munn Avenue on the sheet; the modern Fort Lee Road / Park Avenue junction was excluded.
Water pipe on Walnut marked To New Durham Sta.

Printed sheet 37, 100 ft, two parts divided by a heavy vertical line. Part 1 (left): Teaneck south of Degraw Avenue: Hackensack & Fort Lee Rd, Beech, Chestnut (= Woodbine Street), Elm (= Morningside Terrace), Munn to Maple, Bergen, Park and Lees avenues. Part 2 (right, turned about 72 degrees): River Road, Catalpa to Chestnut avenues between Kipp and North; Lena = Westview Terrace; Teaneck Public School.

sheet-37-2.description: Right half of sheet 37 of the August 1920 Hackensack volume, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page: its north arrow points to the upper right, so River Road runs across the top and the avenues run across the sheet. It covers a district of Teaneck Township north of the Bogota line, from River Road and the Kipp Estate at the top to Chestnut Avenue at the bottom, between Kipp and North. The cross avenues are Catalpa Avenue, Lena, Larch Avenue, Elm Avenue, Linden Avenue and Chestnut Avenue, and Kenwood Place runs between Kipp and North from River Road to Larch Avenue; Kipp Avenue is lettered at the top beyond River Road. The blocks are laid out in house lots, many still vacant, with scattered one- and two-storey frame and stuccoed dwellings and garages. On Lena stands the fire station of a volunteer company with hose cart and chemical engine, and at Elm Avenue and North the Teaneck Public School, heated by steam with electric light. The lots along the right margin are numbered as blocks 152A to 152C and 154. A narrow strip of blocks west of Kipp is cut by the dividing line, and the number 30 marks the adjoining sheet.
notes: Lena is now Westview Terrace; Kipp is Kipp Street, North is North Street, and Linden Avenue is Linden Street here.
Kipp / Linden was hand-picked: the detector paired the part's dividing line with a lot line.
The Chestnut Avenue row is partly covered by the scale bar.
